q: how tall is the statue of liberty
statue of liberty height
how high is the statue of liberty
how big is the statue of liberty
a: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor is 93 meters (305 feet) tall from the ground to the tip of the torch. The statue itself (from heel to torch) is 46 meters (151 feet) tall, and its pedestal and base add another 47 meters. The statue weighs about 225 tonnes, including 31 tonnes of copper, which is about the thickness of two pennies. It was a gift from France, dedicated in 1886, and was designed by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi with the internal iron framework engineered by Gustave Eiffel (of Eiffel Tower fame). Visitors can climb 162 steps to the crown.

q: how long is the amazon river
amazon river length
how many miles long is the amazon
how long is the amazon
a: The Amazon River is about 6,400 kilometers (4,000 miles) long, and recent studies measuring it from its farthest source in the Peruvian Andes give it a length of about 6,400 km, making it a close rival to the Nile for the title of longest river. What is undisputed is that the Amazon carries more water than any other river — about 209,000 cubic meters per second at its mouth, more than the next seven largest rivers combined. It flows from the Andes across Brazil to the Atlantic, and during the wet season it can be up to 40 kilometers (25 miles) wide. The Amazon basin contains the world's largest rainforest.

q: how deep is the ocean
how deep is the ocean in the deepest part
average depth of the ocean
how deep is the deepest ocean
a: The average depth of the ocean is about 3,700 meters (12,100 feet). The deepest point is Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, about 10,935 meters (35,876 feet) below sea level — deeper than Mount Everest is tall. If you placed Everest in Challenger Deep, its summit would still be over 2,000 meters underwater. The first person to reach the bottom of Challenger Deep was Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh in the bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960, followed by James Cameron in 2012. About 80% of the ocean remains unmapped at high resolution.

q: how hot is the sun
what is the temperature of the sun
sun surface temperature
how hot is the suns surface
a: The Sun's surface temperature is about 5,500°C (9,900°F). Its core is much hotter — about 15 million °C (27 million °F), where nuclear fusion converts hydrogen into helium. The Sun's outer atmosphere, the corona, is paradoxically much hotter than the surface, reaching about 1-3 million °C, and scientists are still studying why. The Sun is a middle-aged G-type main-sequence star, about 4.6 billion years old, and it is 149.6 million kilometers (93 million miles) from Earth. It produces energy equivalent to about 4 million tonnes of mass converted per second.

q: how heavy is an elephant
how much does an elephant weigh
elephant weight
how much does an african elephant weigh
a: An African bush elephant, the largest land animal, weighs up to 6 tonnes (13,200 pounds) for a large adult male, with females typically around 3-4 tonnes. Asian elephants are lighter, with males up to about 5 tonnes. A newborn elephant calf weighs about 90-120 kg (200-265 pounds) and is already one of the largest newborns of any land animal. Elephants can eat up to 150 kg of vegetation per day, which helps explain their size. The heaviest elephant ever recorded weighed about 11 tonnes.

q: how long is the great wall of china
great wall of china length
how long is the great wall
how many miles is the great wall
a: The Great Wall of China is about 21,196 kilometers (13,171 miles) long, including all its branches and sections, as measured by a 2012 Chinese government survey. The most famous sections, like Badaling and Mutianyu, were built during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and stretch about 8,850 kilometers. Construction began over 2,000 years ago, starting in the 7th century BC, and successive dynasties added to it. Contrary to myth, the Great Wall is not visible from space with the naked eye. It is the longest human-made structure on Earth and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: how high is mount everest
how tall is mount everest
mount everest height
what is the height of mount everest
a: Mount Everest is 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet) above sea level, as officially re-measured in 2020 by China and Nepal. It is the highest mountain on Earth and one of the Seven Summits. Everest grows about 4 millimeters per year as the Indian tectonic plate continues to push into Asia. It was first summited on 29 May 1953 by Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa of Nepal. Over 340 people have died attempting the climb, and most summits happen in May when the weather window opens. The mountain is called Sagarmatha in Nepali and Chomolungma in Tibetan.

q: how fast can a cheetah run
cheetah top speed
how fast is a cheetah
how fast can cheetahs run
a: A cheetah can run at speeds up to about 100-120 km/h (60-75 mph), making it the fastest land animal. It can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h (62 mph) in about 3 seconds — faster than most sports cars. However, cheetahs can only maintain top speed for about 20-30 seconds before overheating, so they typically cover 200-300 meters per chase. Their bodies are built for speed: a flexible spine, semi-retractable claws for grip, a long tail for balance, and enlarged nostrils and lungs. Cheetahs are found mainly in Africa, with a small population in Iran, and about 7,000 remain in the wild.

q: how tall is the eiffel tower
eiffel tower height
how tall is the eiffel tower
how high is the eiffel tower
a: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is 330 meters (1,083 feet) tall including its antennas, and 300 meters (984 feet) without them. It was built for the 1889 World's Fair by Gustave Eiffel's company and was the world's tallest structure until the Chrysler Building surpassed it in 1930. The tower weighs about 10,100 tonnes and has three levels open to visitors, with restaurants on the first and second levels and a champagne bar at the top. It was almost torn down in 1909 but was saved because its antennas were useful for radio transmission. The tower sways up to about 7 centimeters in the wind, and it expands about 15 centimeters in summer heat.
